title: Committee of Supply – Head B (Attorney-General's Chambers)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head B (Attorney-General's Chambers)

sections.label: Review of Attorney-General's role
sections.summary: The Member filed a cut to suggest reviewing the Attorney-General's role, noting Article 35 gives the Attorney-General two roles requiring different behaviour.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Chairman, I filed this cut to suggest a review of the role of the Attorney-General, with a view to making our legal system even more robust.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Currently, under Article 35 of the Constitution, the Attorney-General is entrusted with two roles that require him to behave quite differently.

sections.label: Splitting Public Prosecutor roles
sections.summary: The Member asks the Government to consider splitting the two roles into two offices so the Public Prosecutor is not the person taking Government instructions in non-criminal matters.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In order to further strengthen the system and shore up the independence of the Public Prosecutor, I ask the Government to consider splitting the two roles I have described, to reside in two different offices, so that the person who is Public Prosecutor is not the same person taking the Government's instructions in non-criminal matters.

sections.label: Suitable period for appointment
sections.summary: The Member says a suitable period could take reference from the Auditor-General's appointment, which under the Constitution is a six-year term.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As to what period is suitable, we could take reference from the period currently set for the appointment for the Auditor-General, which, under the Constitution, is a six-year term.

sections.label: Survey on legal system trust
sections.summary: A survey found 92% had trust and confidence in Singapore's legal system, 96% agreed Singapore is governed by the rule of law, and 90% trusted the Attorney-General's Chambers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Ninety-two percent said they had trust and confidence in Singapore's legal system, and that the system is fair and efficient.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Ninety-six percent agreed that Singapore is governed by the rule of law.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The same survey also revealed that 90% said they had trust and confidence in the Attorney-General's Chambers.

sections.label: Dual-key appointment system
sections.summary: The Member states that, on top of that, there is a dual-key system for the appointment of the Attorney-General.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Second, on top of that, we have a dual-key system for the appointment of the Attorney-General.

sections.label: Confirmation on separation principle
sections.summary: The Member asks the Senior Minister of State to confirm he acknowledges the principle of separation between the Chief Prosecutor and the Chief Government legal advisor is taken in other jurisdictions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: First, may I just get the Senior Minister of State's confirmation that he actually acknowledges that this principle of separation between the Chief Prosecutor and the Chief Government legal advisor is taken in other jurisdictions?

sections.label: Attorney-General short term continuity
sections.summary: A short-term Attorney-General appointment means his contract lapses and service ends, so continuity in his term is suggested for public interest matters.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: But at the same time as well, if the Attorney-General is appointed for a short term, then his contract will just lapse and, in that sense, he will be removed after a short period of time or his service will be terminated.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: So, is it not worth considering actually to introduce a certain continuity in the term of the Attorney-General, so that he can see through certain matters that are of concern to public interest?

sections.label: Integrity and high-profile prosecutions
sections.summary: The system is shown working through persons of utmost integrity and high-profile prosecutions conducted with no fear and no favour.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: But more than that, we also look at the individual, persons of integrity, utmost integrity, discharging those functions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And finally also, the proof of the pudding is really in the eating – in looking at the conduct, looking at the fact that, with no fear and no favour, there have been high-profile prosecutions, including those that I have outlined, which demonstrate that our system is working.
